question: Are the next two independent ideal D4 prerequisites a realizable simple red-edge loop and an already stateful action-feedback interface, or must either branch stop before full-law/noisy sampling?
role: Two-branch deterministic prerequisite audit, not a new measurement law or performance experiment
source_basis: Jing Appendix A.2/A.4 red-X strings and flux-free projectors

matrix.method: For every frozen red edge, find the shortest endpoint path with that edge deleted; these edge-deletion searches cover every cycle candidate for the global minimum. Report minimum length, a deterministic canonical witness edge tuple, edge uniqueness and vertex degree two. A graph-only result is not an exact charge law.

Audit the pinned public runner signatures and frozen history builder/provider for a third ordered projector block and propagation of a realized correction plus postselected state into the next physical/first observation. Mark present only if both are explicit; otherwise mark absent and identify the first missing interface.

independent_unit: One deterministic pinned L=2 graph and one pinned source-interface audit; no sampling units or uncertainty interval
acceptance: The minimum cycle is verified by all-edge deletion shortest-path searches and degree-two closure
The stateful verdict follows explicit signatures/data flow, not presumed physical dynamics
No exact loop public law, 3-round D4 kernel, histories, arms, bootstrap, threshold or schedule claim is made
stop_rule: Fail closed on hash drift, graph ambiguity, cycle nonclosure or unclear data flow. An absent stateful interface stops its dependent numeric kernel and noisy schedule work; the independent loop-geometry audit continues.
